BodyTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs.blurb: Maximum body turn rate (degrees per second, default 30) allowed when Vector first accepts a brand-new pet detection into PetWorld. If the body was spinning faster than this at the camera frame’s timestamp, that new cat/dog ID is discarded so motion blur does not invent pets.
BodyTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs.detail: Read only in PetWorld::Update for IDs not already known. Existing tracked pets are always kept even if the robot is turning. Together with HeadTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs, the check is enabled only if at least one of the two thresholds is > 0; set both ≤ 0 to disable the rotating-too-fast gate for new pets. Degrees are converted to radians for ImuHistory::WasRotatingTooFast. Sibling defaults match faces (10°/s head, 30°/s body) and marker body threshold.

HeadTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs.blurb: Maximum head tilt/pitch rate (degrees per second, default 10) allowed when first accepting a new pet ID into PetWorld. Fast head motion at detection time blocks that new ID so shaky frames do not spawn false cats or dogs.
HeadTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs.detail: Same gate as BodyTurnSpeedThreshPet_degs: only new IDs (not already in _knownPets) consult IMU history; already-known pets keep updating. WasRotatingTooFast is true if either head or body rate exceeds its threshold. Set both head and body thresholds ≤ 0 to turn the whole check off. For tracked detections, NumImuDataToLookBackPet also widens the IMU samples examined around the frame time.

NumImuDataToLookBackPet.blurb: How many IMU samples before the image timestamp to also check for too-fast motion when accepting a new pet that is already marked “being tracked” by the Omron detector (default 5). First-sight detections (not tracked yet) always use look-back 0.
NumImuDataToLookBackPet.detail: Passed as the last argument to ImuHistory::WasRotatingTooFast only when petDetection.IsBeingTracked() is true (OMCV DET_METHOD_TRACKED_MIDDLE). For pure first detections look-back is forced to 0, so only samples at/near that timestamp matter. Larger values are stricter (more history can fail the gate); 0 only samples around t. Only matters when body or head turn thresholds are > 0 so the rotating-too-fast check is enabled.

Pets.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::Pets so every scheduled vision pass can run cat/dog face detection (Omron OMCV Pet Detector). Off by default as a console override; production behaviors subscribe the mode when they need pet awareness.
Pets.detail: Created dynamically for every VisionMode under category Vision.General.VisionModes (SetupVisionModeConsoleVars). When the bool flips, VisionComponent enables/disables the mode and DevOnly self-subscribes/unsubscribes so Pets is actually on the schedule even if no behavior requested it. When mode runs, VisionSystem::DetectPets calls PetTracker on the gray (optionally masked) image; results go to PetWorld (RobotObservedPet broadcast, viz ovals, DAS on first sight). Behaviors such as PetDetection, FindFaces, TrackPetFaceAction, and several reactions request Pets at Low/Med/High/Standard. Schedule cost is relatively high (relativeCost 16 in visionScheduleMediator_config). Masking: pet search blacks out rects already used by earlier detectors in the same frame (e.g. faces).
Pets.howTo: 1) Toggle Pets on in console (Vision.General.VisionModes). 2) Point Vector at a cat or dog face of reasonable size (~60–240 px per vision_config PetTracker). 3) Optionally lower RuntimePetDetectionThreshold if detections are sparse. 4) Watch PetWorld viz / RobotObservedPet or WebViz detections; use Body/Head turn thresholds if spinning invents ghosts.

paths.notes: PetTracker block: MaxPets 4, DetectionThreshold 900 (0–1000), Min/MaxFaceSize 60/240, search cycles, track lost/steadiness. Schedule: Pets low=4 med=2 high=1 standard=1, relativeCost 16.

RuntimePetDetectionThreshold.blurb: Live override for how confident the Omron pet detector must be (0–1000) before reporting a cat or dog. Default −1 means “leave the value from vision_config.json alone” (stock DetectionThreshold 900). Set ≥ 0 to push a new threshold into the detector on the next pet Update.
RuntimePetDetectionThreshold.detail: CONSOLE_VAR_RANGED −1…1000 under Vision.PetDetection. PetTracker::Init loads DetectionThreshold from JSON and calls OMCV_PD_SetThreshold once. On each Update, if this console value is ≥ 0 and differs from the last applied runtime threshold, it re-calls OMCV_PD_SetThreshold and caches the new value. Lower values accept weaker detections (more hits, more false positives); higher values are stricter. Only affects the classic PetTracker path (VisionMode::Pets), not neural-net people/hands. Failed SetThreshold returns an error from Update.
RuntimePetDetectionThreshold.howTo: 1) Ensure Pets mode is running. 2) Set RuntimePetDetectionThreshold to a value 0–1000 (try ~700–850 if stock 900 misses pets). 3) Point at a pet and watch detections. 4) Set back to −1 to stop overriding (threshold stays at last applied value until process restart reloads JSON).

paths.notes: PetTracker.DetectionThreshold default 900 (0–1000). Console −1 = do not override at runtime.
